node.title: Re: Why can't some of my modules do log output to a file?
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
it should work, right?

In addition to the comments by the others, I would suggest using [doc://flock], turning on [doc://Data::Dumper]'s Useqq option, and adding more error checking.

use warnings; use strict; use Fcntl qw/:flock/; use Data::Dumper; sub write_log { my ($file, $obj) = @_; open my $fh, '>>', $file or die "open $file: $!"; flock($fh, LOCK_EX) or die "flock $file: $!"; print {$fh} Data::Dumper->new([$obj])->Useqq(1)->Dump or die "print $file: $!"; close $fh or die "close $file: $!"; } write_log("/tmp/log.txt", {hello=>"world"});

If that didn't work or die, personally I would assume the code really wasn't being run, or perhaps that some other process was messing with the logfile. (Note it's been a while since I've used [doc://flock] on Windows, but I assume you're on *NIX based on your filename.)

There's definitely nothing wrong with the logfile

Well now that you've said that, I have to ask ;-) Are you sure? SELinux? Are all the processes spawned by the script running as the same user?
